clue.text: Change in fares today — travellers should pay attention to it

definitions.text: travellers should pay attention to it

indicators.note: a change in the words means their letters are rearranged into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A notice about a new fare structure that passengers ought to read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change in' tells you to rearrange the ten letters of FARES TODAY. The surface suggests ticket prices, but the definition is the safety of people on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Road users of every kind are expected to heed the rules for keeping safe on highways.

clue.text: Place for holiday or taking it easy outside

indicators.note: the word for resting goes outside, wrapped around the other piece

parts.note: taking it easy means having a rest
taken as written

explanation.surface: A holiday spot, or simply a lazy day spent outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' looks like part of the lounging-about picture, resting in the open air, but it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaside town or ski village where people go on vacation is called a holiday spot of this kind.

clue.text: A British way found in other places

parts.note: a road is a way

explanation.surface: A Briton walking a path through foreign lands.
explanation.definitionFit: Being overseas or in foreign countries means being somewhere other than home.

clue.text: Sergeant major very enthusiastic about music, making a lot of money

parts.note: to be all for something is to be keen on it
a tune is a piece of music

explanation.surface: An army sergeant major who loves music turns it into a lucrative sideline.
explanation.walkthrough: ALL FOR is the idiom 'all for it', meaning strongly in favour.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a large sum of cash, as when something costs a packet.

clue.text: Trip in autumn to us

definitions.meaning: to trip is to stumble, or a stumble itself
Americans call the season after summer by this name, 'us' read as US

explanation.walkthrough: 'us' hides the US: read it as the United States, where the season is named for falling leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A stumble ends on the ground, and the American word for the leaf-dropping season is the same word.

clue.text: Not crossing the circle line? It's irrelevant

definitions.meaning: a straight line that touches a circle at one point without cutting through it
only loosely connected to the matter in hand

explanation.surface: A remark about a London Underground route turns out to be beside the point.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle line is a London Underground route; here it is a geometric line that grazes a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: A geometric touching line meets a curve at one point only, and a remark that merely touches the subject is off-topic.

clue.text: Shout heard at sea from a small vessel

parts.note: a hoy is a small coastal sailing boat or barge

explanation.surface: A hail from a little boat on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: A hoy is an old word for a small coastal vessel, worth knowing for crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors call out this greeting to hail another ship.

clue.text: What makes me very angry, breaking garden tool? That's natural

indicators.note: breaking into the tool word means the other pieces sit inside it

parts.note: a hoe is a garden tool for weeding
taken as written
mad means very angry

explanation.surface: Someone fuming at a snapped hoe, consoled that it was bound to happen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' is the container signal. 'What makes' and 'That's' are link words; the surface makes 'natural' sound like resignation over a broken tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Food made in your own kitchen rather than a factory is thought of as wholesome and free of additives.

clue.text: Ambivalent answer from French author, gripped by desire and love

indicators.note: the author is held inside the word for desire

parts.note: yen means a longing or desire
George Sand was a French novelist
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A French writer, torn between longing and love, cannot give a straight reply.
explanation.walkthrough: George Sand is a pen name of the 19th-century French novelist Aurore Dupin.
explanation.definitionFit: A reply that is both positive and negative shows mixed feelings.

clue.text: Policy on student group to simplify procedure

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: a stream is a group of pupils of similar ability in a school
a line is a policy, as in the party line

explanation.surface: A school policy on how classes are grouped, meant to make admin easier.
explanation.walkthrough: Streaming is the British school practice of grouping pupils by ability.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a process more efficient by cutting unnecessary steps.

clue.text: A doctor's prophetic work

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a doctor; with the 's it gives MOS

explanation.surface: A physician's writings that predict the future.
explanation.walkthrough: MO stands for medical officer, an army doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A book of the Old Testament named after one of the minor prophets.

clue.text: Being unable to cope with strain, a job for analyst

definitions.text: Being unable to cope with strain
definitions.meaning: collapsing under stress, mentally or physically
an analyst splits a thing into its parts for study

explanation.surface: Someone cracking under pressure, and the therapist who must take them apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A nervous collapse, and also the analysis of something into its component parts.

clue.text: Sceptical thing to say about friend

parts.note: re means about or concerning
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: Raising an eyebrow at someone's tale about a pal.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of disbelief, said when doubting what one hears.

clue.text: Boat operator getting ridiculously merry, put in cooler

indicators.note: the scrambled letters are placed inside the word for a cooler

parts.note: a fan cools you down

indicators.note: used in a silly way, the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A boatman who gets absurdly drunk and ends up in the cooler, slang for prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ridiculously' gives ERRYM and 'put in' is the container signal. 'Cooler' is slang for a jail cell, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who carries passengers across water for a fee.

clue.text: Rinse cup so badly in the kitchen

indicators.note: done badly, the letters come out in a muddle

explanation.surface: Someone doing a poor job of washing a mug at the sink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' scrambles RINSE CUP SO. Orchestral players call the percussion section 'the kitchen', for its pots and pans of drums and cymbals.
explanation.definitionFit: Orchestral slang names the drums and cymbals section after a room full of clattering pans.

clue.text: Part of our capital in terrible danger after business opening

indicators.note: the scrambled word follows the two short pieces

parts.note: CO is short for company, a business
a vent is an opening

indicators.note: made terrible, the word is wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: Part of London is at grave risk once a new firm opens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges DANGER to give GARDEN. Covent Garden is a district of central London, once its fruit and flower market.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-known district in the heart of London, the British capital.

clue.text: Agonised dreadfully in city just north of the border

definitions.text: city just north of the border

indicators.note: treated dreadfully, the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone suffering terribly in a frontier town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadfully' rearranges AGONISED. The city lies in California just north of the Mexican border.
explanation.definitionFit: A Californian port near Tijuana, on the US side of the frontier with Mexico.

clue.text: One who takes union activity beyond the legal limit?

definitions.text: One who takes union activity beyond the legal limit?

parts.words: One who takes union activity beyond the legal limit?
parts.note: union reads as trade-union action, but means marriage: a person wed to more spouses than the law allows

explanation.surface: A militant shop steward pushing a strike past what the law permits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' suggests trade unions; it means marriage, and the legal limit is one spouse at a time.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who marries while still legally wed to someone else.

clue.text: Special art I put into complicated acrostic by no means common

indicators.note: the first scrambled group goes inside the second
made complicated, the letters are tangled up
special here means rearranged into an unusual order

explanation.surface: A clever word puzzle with an artful twist, hardly ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Special' gives RATI, 'complicated' gives ARISTOCC, and 'put into' sets RATI before that group's final C.
explanation.definitionFit: Belonging to the nobility, the very opposite of the common people.

clue.text: She was barely able to get tax relief on horse

definitions.text: She was barely able to get tax relief on horse

parts.words: She was barely able to get tax relief on horse
parts.note: the legendary lady of Coventry who rode naked through the town so her husband would lift a harsh tax

explanation.surface: A woman who could scarcely win a tax break on her horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barely' seems to mean 'only just'; it means naked. Legend says the 11th-century noblewoman rode unclothed through Coventry to have a tax lifted.
explanation.definitionFit: The noblewoman of English legend whose naked ride won the townspeople relief from taxation.

clue.text: Stuck in weed, dog lost the ball

indicators.note: the shortened animal goes inside the word for the plant
the dog loses something, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: a ball is round, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A dog's ball has vanished into the weeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' leaves DG and 'in' is the container signal; the surface pictures a dog hunting for its ball in the undergrowth.
explanation.definitionFit: Jammed firmly in place, unable to move.

clue.text: Figure out the problem disturbing 16

indicators.note: disturbing the letters mixes them up

parts.note: the answer to 16 Down, a Californian city

explanation.surface: Working out what is troubling a person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbing' rearranges the letters of the answer to 16, the city.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor identifies an illness from its symptoms, working out what is wrong.

clue.text: Cut head off Italian gentleman

indicators.note: with its head off, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: signore is Italian for a gentleman or sir

explanation.surface: Beheading an Italian man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like an instruction to chop, but it is the definition: to snub someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut someone is to snub them, deliberately pretending not to see them.

clue.text: Son topping academic stream is a fraud

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge, the university city

explanation.surface: A boy coming top of the academic set is a cheat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'academic stream' means the River Cam in Cambridge, not a school ability group.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindle or con trick is a dishonest deception.

clue.text: English cricket team taking little time to get out

parts.note: a cricket team has eleven players, XI in Roman numerals
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: England's cricketers taking a short break before leaving the field.
explanation.walkthrough: A cricket side is often written XI, the Roman numeral for its eleven players.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave or depart from a place.

clue.text: Publishing record being beaten

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
losing means being beaten

explanation.surface: A record label releasing an album that is a flop.
explanation.definitionFit: Revealing or making public information that was hidden.

clue.text: German taking part of bible and repeating it back

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, part of the Bible

indicators.note: back means the repeated piece is read in reverse

parts.note: repeating it gives the Old Testament abbreviation a second time

explanation.surface: A German reader taking a passage of scripture and reciting it in reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: Otto is a typical German man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A common masculine first name in Germany, borne by Bismarck.

clue.text: Soloist? Doesn't sound like it!

parts.note: a lone performer who plays several instruments at once, so they sound like a group

explanation.surface: Doubting that a performer is really playing alone.
explanation.walkthrough: The performer is solo yet sounds like a whole group, since one person plays many instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: A street entertainer playing several instruments at once, single-handedly.
